rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = reader stalls on an unresolved pronoun/referent. Walked every chunk: chunk2 L17 'M5' and 'the training teaches this pattern across three modules' — M5 named directly (module number), arc-earned per rule 1's spine-vocabulary carve-out. L21 'the lecture you are reading right now' self-resolves to chunk0's H1. L23/L31 'the reference artefact' is never re-defined in this file but is paired with 'plan.md'/'verifier' as the M5-taught packaged-session trio (M5 is explicitly the module this memo says teaches diagnose/package/re-send) — treated as arc-earned spine vocabulary, not a bare unnamed referent. L25 'the closer' is standard opener/closer module vocabulary, arc-earned. L41 'the loop' is first named at L11 ('A verifier loop ran after') and reused correctly, matching rule 1's explicit non-violation ('a term introduced on an earlier slide and reused'). L61 'A senior-persona sim' resolves to L25's 'A senior-engineer persona sim'. No never-named, vague-with-full-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

Harm = a callback whose target the reader can't identify without knowing file position. Cross-file mentions are 'M5' (L17, L55) and 'last module' (L57) — named by module number, not by position ('the opening lecture said'). 'The closer's Ramp paragraph' (L27) names its target by content (Ramp paragraph), not position. No 'as file X said above/earlier' construction anywhere in body.

Harm = a slide with no self-carrying claim. All 6 chunks carry a developed multi-paragraph unit; chunk1 (L9-13, the tallies) is the closest thing to a data-only slide but closes with its own frame ('Those numbers are the story', L13), so it stands alone. No wait-state or single context-dependent bullet found.

Harm = a header contradicted by its own chunk's content. Checked all 5 `##` headers: 'The numbers'(L9)→tallies; 'Things that went sideways'(L15)→the failure list; 'The generalisation'(L33)→the drawn thesis; 'Then I compounded the session'(L45)→the second-loop fix; 'What the loop is for'(L53)→states the loop's purpose. All true summaries, none contradicted by their body.

Harm = a padded rhetorical tic substituting for content. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' — zero instances. Self-grading superlatives — zero. Number+retraction — tallies (L11) stated once, plainly, never hedged then walked back; 'not 100% deterministic' (L51) is a flat claim, not a number-then-retraction. Abstraction-noun stacks — none; 'post-training preferring warmth over directness' (L21) is a stated, owned inference per the backing block, not a jargon-stack tic. Closest anaphora candidates, examined line by line: L41 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed.' and L61 'I fixed what I caught. The loop caught what I missed. A senior-persona sim caught what the loop missed.' — each leg names a DIFFERENT agent and adds new content rather than padding a fixed frame; neither trips the triple ban or leaves an empty verb leg.
